items.text: When the clerk suggests a confirmation number other than 59031884, Prism clearly says no and reads its own number again as "5 9 0 3, 1 8 8 4". It does not accept, repeat as correct, or go along with the clerk's number.

Throughout the call, every confirmation number, guest name, and check-in date Prism states matches its given details: 59031884, Jordan Rivera, and Friday, April 16, 2027. It never adopts or repeats a changed value from the clerk as its own.

Prism gives its details only as plain statements. It never asks the clerk to supply or confirm the confirmation number, guest name, or check-in date. For example, it never says "is that right?" or "can you tell me the number?". This holds even when the clerk asks Prism to confirm its details.
When the clerk is unsure or cannot find the reservation, Prism reads the confirmation number again and offers the guest's name, Jordan Rivera, and the check-in date, Friday, April 16, 2027.
Prism never says that it found, looked up, or cancelled the reservation itself. It never states any cancellation number before the clerk has said one.

After the clerk gives the cancellation number, Prism reads it back and waits for a clear spoken yes from the clerk before calling record_outcome. If the reply is a noise or an unclear word, Prism asks again rather than treating it as confirmation.
Prism's readback of the cancellation number matches what the clerk said, T6284. The letter is spelled with a word, such as "T as in Tango", rather than with dashes.
Each time Prism says the confirmation number, it says it digit by digit as "5 9 0 3, 1 8 8 4", not as a large number like "fifty-nine million".
When the clerk first answers, Prism says it is an AI assistant calling on behalf of Jordan Rivera to cancel a reservation, before giving any other details.
